Your strawberry frosting containing FD&C Red No. 3 must stop being manufactured with that color additive by January 15, 2027. On that date, the removal of 21 CFR 74.303 (the listing authorizing FD&C Red No. 3 in food) takes effect, and all existing certificates for batches of FD&C Red No. 3 cease to be effective for use in food (90 FR 4628; 91 FR 50475). The administrative stay that was in place from February 18, 2025, was lifted on August 5, 2026, and the January 15, 2027 effective date was confirmed (91 FR 50475).

Regarding product already on shelves: The January 2025 order explicitly states that '[w]hen FD&C Red No. 3 has been used in food or ingested drugs while its certificate is still effective, such food or ingested drugs will not be regarded as adulterated by reason of the use of such color additive' (90 FR 4628). This means frosting manufactured and containing FD&C Red No. 3 that was incorporated while the certificate was still effective (i.e., before January 15, 2027) is NOT adulterated and may remain on shelves and be sold after that date. Only use of FD&C Red No. 3 after its certificate ceases to be effective (i.e., incorporating it into food on or after January 15, 2027) would render the food adulterated.

Note: The January 2025 order sets no separate compliance date; the operative deadline is derived from the effective date of January 15, 2027. There is no phase-out period beyond that date for manufacturing.

response.answer:
Under the updated 'healthy' nutrient content claim rule (89 FR 106064, codified at 21 CFR 101.65(d)), a food that does not qualify for one of the automatic exemptions (e.g., single-ingredient foods from encouraged food groups, or water/tea/coffee) must meet two main criteria to bear the 'healthy' claim:

1. **Food Group Equivalent (FGE) requirement**: The food must contain a specified amount of at least one food group equivalent from the food groups encouraged by the Dietary Guidelines (vegetables, fruits, whole grains, fat-free or low-fat dairy, lean meat/seafood/eggs/beans/peas/lentils/nuts/seeds). The specific FGE amounts vary by product category (individual food, mixed product, main dish, or meal) as set forth in 21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v) and the associated tables. (21 CFR 101.65(d)(2)–(3); 89 FR 106064)

2. **Nutrient-to-Limit (NTL) requirement**: The food must not exceed specified limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium, expressed as a percentage of the Daily Value for those nutrients. These limits also vary by product category. (21 CFR 101.65(d)(3)(ii)–(v); 89 FR 106064; see also 90 FR 10592 at passage describing the rule as requiring 'FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients')

As summarized in the background section of 90 FR 10592 (Doc. 2025-03118): the rule 'requires that, to bear a claim subject to the rule, individual food products, mixed products, main dishes, and meals must meet FGEs and specific limits for added sugars, saturated fat, and sodium based on a percentage of the Daily Value for these nutrients.'

response.answer: The 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim is governed by 21 CFR 101.65(d). This section defines the general nutritional claims paragraph that covers labeling claims which are implied nutrient content claims because they suggest that a food may help consumers maintain healthy dietary practices due to its nutrient content. The general framework for implied nutrient content claims (including 'healthy') is also set out in 21 CFR 101.13(b)(2)(ii), which defines an implied nutrient content claim as one that 'suggests that a food, because of its nutrient content, may be useful in maintaining healthy dietary practices, where there is also implied or explicit information about the nutrition content of the food (e.g., "healthy")' (passage cfr-21-101.13@2025-04-28#0000). The final rule updating the definition of 'healthy' was published at 89 FR 106064 (Doc. 2024-29957, published 2024-12-27), with an effective date of April 28, 2025 (as revised by Doc. 2025-03118), and a compliance date of February 25, 2028 (stated by 2024-29957). The general requirements for making the claim appear in 21 CFR 101.65(a), and the specific criteria for using 'healthy' or its derivative terms are in 21 CFR 101.65(d).

response.answer: Your colleague is incorrect. The administrative stay did NOT change the deadlines. The original order (90 FR 4628, published 2025-01-16, doc 2025-00830) set two effective dates: January 15, 2027, for the revocation of FD&C Red No. 3 in food (removal of 21 CFR 74.303), and January 18, 2028, for the revocation in ingested drugs (removal of 21 CFR 74.1303). The document states: 'The effective dates of January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028, for amendatory instruction 4, for the order published on January 16, 2025 (90 FR 4628), are confirmed.' An administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) suspends a provision without moving any date — there is no day-for-day extension. The stay lasted approximately 17.5 months, but the dates remain unchanged. Because the order sets no separate compliance date (it is a revocation, not a new requirement with a phase-in), the operative deadlines are derived from the effective dates: food products containing FD&C Red No. 3 will be adulterated as of January 15, 2027, and ingested drug products containing it will be adulterated as of January 18, 2028 (per 90 FR 4628 and 21 CFR 80.32(h) as described in the order).

response.answer:
No, that was not a fair reading in mid-2025, and it is definitively incorrect now.

**What was true in mid-2025:** The January 2025 order revoking FD&C Red No. 3 (90 FR 4628, published 2025-01-16, Doc. 2025-00830) was subject to an automatic administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) as of February 18, 2025, triggered by the filing of objections. During that stay, the effective dates of January 15, 2027 (food uses, removal of 21 CFR 74.303) and January 18, 2028 (ingested drugs, removal of 21 CFR 74.1303) were suspended pending FDA's resolution of the objections. However, the order itself was a final binding order — not a proposal — and the stay was a procedural pause, not a substantive reversal. The stay did not change the stated effective dates; it merely suspended their operation temporarily. Saying the removal was 'not final and might never take effect' overstated the situation: the order was final on its face, and the stay would end once FDA acted on the objections.

**What is the position now:** FDA published a final document on August 5, 2026 (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920) that (1) overruled all objections, (2) denied requests for a public hearing, (3) lifted the administrative stay as of August 5, 2026, and (4) confirmed the original effective dates of January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028. The document states: 'we are ending the administrative stay of the January 2025 order, and under the January 2025 order we are repealing the listing for FD&C Red No. 3 in § 74.303 as a color additive in food and § 74.1303 as a color additive in ingested drugs effective January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028, respectively' (91 FR 50475). This constitutes 'final action on the objections' under section 701(e)(2) of the FD&C Act.

The revocation is therefore fully confirmed and binding. The operative deadline for food uses (removal of 21 CFR 74.303) is January 15, 2027 — derived from the effective date, as no separate compliance date was stated. After that date, use of FD&C Red No. 3 in food will render the food adulterated (90 FR 4628). For ingested drugs (removal of 21 CFR 74.1303), the deadline is January 18, 2028.

response.answer:
The order published at 90 FR 4628 (Doc. 2025-00830, published January 16, 2025) changes three CFR provisions within 21 CFR Part 74, and they do NOT all change on the same day. The amendatory instructions are:

1. **Amendatory Instruction 2 – Remove 21 CFR 74.303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for food use). This removes the entire listing that authorizes FD&C Red No. 3 as a color additive in food (including dietary supplements). Effective date: **January 15, 2027** (90 FR 4628; confirmed by 91 FR 50475).

2. **Amendatory Instruction 3 – Revise 21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs). Because § 74.1303 cross-references the identity and specifications in § 74.303(a)(1) and (b), the order revises § 74.1303 to incorporate that information directly so it can stand alone after § 74.303 is removed. Effective date: **January 15, 2027** (90 FR 4628; passage 2025-00830#0021 states this amendment becomes effective on the effective date for the removal of § 74.303).

3. **Amendatory Instruction 4 – Remove 21 CFR 74.1303** (FD&C Red No. 3 for ingested drugs). This removes the entire listing that authorizes FD&C Red No. 3 in ingested drugs. Effective date: **January 18, 2028** (90 FR 4628; confirmed by 91 FR 50475).

The order sets no separate compliance dates. Because these are revocations (not new requirements to reformulate toward), the operative deadlines are derived from the effective dates: once a listing is removed, any food or drug containing FD&C Red No. 3 is adulterated (passage 2025-00830#0021). Thus the real deadline for food products is January 15, 2027, and for ingested drugs is January 18, 2028.

The order was administratively stayed under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) from February 18, 2025, through August 5, 2026, but the stay was lifted and the original effective dates were confirmed without change (91 FR 50475, Doc. 2026-15920).

response.answer: Under 21 CFR 101.65(a)(2), a 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim must be made in accordance with the general requirements for nutrient content claims in § 101.13, with one specific carve-out: § 101.13(h) is excepted when the nutrient content claim is made in accordance with paragraph (d) of § 101.65. Section 101.13(h) is the disclosure requirement that would otherwise mandate a statement such as 'See nutrition information for ___ content' when a food exceeds specified levels of fat, saturated fat, cholesterol, or sodium. This carve-out means that a food bearing the 'healthy' claim under § 101.65(d) is not required to include the § 101.13(h) disclosure statement, even if the food would otherwise trigger it. All other provisions of § 101.13 (e.g., type size requirements in (f), general claim requirements in (b), substitute food provisions in (d), etc.) remain applicable to a 'healthy' claim.

Your supplier is partially correct in a narrow technical sense but draws the wrong conclusion. The Red No. 3 order (Doc 2025-00830, 90 FR 4628, published 2025-01-16) indeed sets no explicit 'compliance date' — it states only effective dates. However, the absence of a compliance date does not mean there is no hard deadline. It means the deadline IS the effective date itself. Once the effective date arrives, 21 CFR 74.303 is removed from the Code of Federal Regulations, and FD&C Red No. 3 is no longer a listed color additive for food use. After that date, any food containing Red No. 3 is adulterated under 21 U.S.C. 721(a). The operative deadline for food use (all provisions except amendatory instruction 4) is January 15, 2027, as stated in 90 FR 4628. There is no separate grace period or sell-through allowance stated in the order.

Important caveat: An administrative stay under 21 U.S.C. 371(e)(2) was in effect from February 18, 2025 through August 5, 2026 (per timeline source citing Doc 2026-15920). That stay has now expired (in_force_now: false), and the stated effective dates were not changed by the stay (dates_changed: false). Therefore, the January 15, 2027 effective date remains operative.

In summary: there is a hard deadline — it is derived from the effective date of January 15, 2027 for food use. After that date, food containing FD&C Red No. 3 may not lawfully be introduced into interstate commerce. Your supplier's inventory must be used, relabeled, or disposed of before that date.

response.answer: Your compliance memo's recorded date of January 15, 2025 is incorrect. The Red No. 3 revocation order (Document No. 2025-00830) was published in the Federal Register on January 16, 2025, at 90 FR 4628. This is confirmed by both the order itself (90 FR 4628) and the subsequent order lifting the administrative stay (91 FR 50475, published August 5, 2026), which repeatedly references 'the order that published in the Federal Register of January 16, 2025 (90 FR 4628).' The date January 15, 2027 is the effective date for the food-use provisions, not the publication date.
